reflection.review:
5 of 5 attempts completed (1 theory/measurement, 4 optimizer incl. 1 debug).
0 records moved. Board unchanged: reg3_250 39.95 / sycamore_m20 61.544 /
reg3_1000 135.75 / rqc_97_m24 106.47 (all `ref:treesa-inf`).

- 026 (theory): **Theorem 1 (sum-form isoperimetric-profile LB) proven and
  validated**; but the unconstrained bound COLLAPSES to the max-form (<1 bit
  above balanced-separator: 30.81 vs 30 on reg3, 47.17 vs 47 on sycamore) —
  the relaxation admits a maximally-skewed adversary tree. On the frontier
  tree's own profile the sum-form explains 93–96% of tc. Fix identified:
  balance-constrained (dyadic-window) DP, provably > 53 on sycamore.
- 027 (profile-aware SA): scored 40.114/61.598, no records. Pre-registered
  null, with an inverted finding: lower-tc trees have FATTER near-max
  shelves (reg3: peak 37→36 but near-max count 7→18) — flops are conserved
  across profile reshaping. Global sharpened-energy variant stalls (bulk
  gradient vanishes); local-dtc formulation ties the plain control exactly.
- 028 (scale generalist): scored 140.78/108.17 — its local bests (133.57 /
  106.30) did not replicate. Throughput 5–6×10^5 moves/s; top-decile-only
  targeting failed (systematic sweep essential; decile boost helps as a
  layer).
- 029 (scale seeds): scored 136.40/106.47 (rqc tie to 0.004). Seed-quality
  hypothesis refuted (hot anneals forget inits; warm preservation needed).
  **Discovered a harness bug**: the scorer's recursion limit silently
  rejected trees taller than ~475 — precisely the deep MPS-like trees good
  RQC orders need. Scorer fixed (iterative walk + raised limit), all five
  negative controls re-rejected, manifest updated.
- 030 (debug, parent 029): unblocked warm path locally beats the rqc
  record (106.284, height-506 tree) but the scored run landed 106.996 —
  not replicated.

Budget: 5/5 slots used; authorized_rounds now 0. Overrides: none this
cycle (scorer fix is a harness correction, self-test re-passed).

reflection.literature:
Nothing in `.knowledge/` treats profile/sum-form bounds for contraction
cost or reports the fat-shelf conservation behavior; both appear novel.
The scale-variance lesson matches the multi-seed methodology in
[gray_2020_hyper] (they report distributions, not single runs — our
protocol should too at scale). The harness-bug case study extends the
methodological thread (Lipton–Steinhardt style) with an
instrument-bias example.
